title: From a Napkin Contract to $1.1 Billion
description:
Why was a soccer star's first contract written on a napkin?

Sources:
- Wikipedia: Lionel Messi: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi
- Wikipedia: Forbes list of the world's highest-paid athletes: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes_list_of_the_world%27s_highest-paid_athletes

From Wikipedia (Lionel Messi): at 10 he was diagnosed with a growth hormone deficiency; at 13, in December 2000, Barcelona's first-team director wrote a contract on a paper napkin; in 2018 he was the first footballer to pass EUR 100 million in a year (EUR 126 million); in 2026 he appeared on the World's Billionaires list with a $1.1 billion net worth. Forbes 2026 (Wikipedia: highest-paid athletes): $140 million, $70 million salary and $70 million endorsements. Not financial advice.

#shorts #messi #soccer #howtheymakemoney
loop: So next time you grab a napkin, ask yourself:
cta: Messi or Ronaldo? Comment your pick.

scenes.narration: Why was a soccer star's first contract written on a napkin?
But at ten, doctors found a growth problem. Treatment cost money every month.
Then, at thirteen, Barcelona wanted him. No paper nearby. So, a napkin.
Then by 2018, he made history. The first player past 100 million euros a year.
Just this year, he joined the billionaires list. 1.1 billion dollars.
